workItem: Project the canonical web-application version in the public mobile sideboard and replace unsupported realtime-latency/security marketing claims with evidence-backed current-main status wording.
workItemDE: Kanonische Webanwendungsversion im öffentlichen Sideboard anzeigen und unbelegte Echtzeit-Latenz-/Sicherheitsangaben durch belegbare Current-Main-Angaben ersetzen.
priorityReason: Public footer currently exposes a hard-coded latency promise and conflates transport security with MiCA; the Owner requested current-version visibility and factual current-main correlation.
scopeBoundary: Version authority remains package.json#version and is projected through Release/clientVersion.ts; no second version literal is introduced.
No market-data provider, entitlement, scoring, licensing, security-control, compliance authority, Render configuration or production deployment is changed.
The sideboard does not claim guaranteed realtime or sub-45ms latency without dataset/provider entitlement evidence.
MiCA remains a regulatory/governance guideline and is not presented as a transport security standard.
acceptanceCriteria: Webanwendung version appears immediately above the market-data feed row and derives from CAPITAL_AI_VERSION_LABEL.
The public sideboard contains no Sub-45ms latency guarantee and no 'SSL 256-Bit • MiCA' security-standard claim.
Feed wording is provider-dependent, security wording reflects HTTPS/CSP, and MiCA is clearly separated as regulatory guidance.
Focused version-projection regression test and required exact-head checks pass.
No changed-file or advisory-claim overlap exists with open PRs.
releaseCondition: Coordination metadata is released when the associated work is merged, closed, superseded or abandoned.

evidence.openWriterOverlap: PASS — merged PR #1347 moved main only in OPS Auth-Control paths; no changed-file overlap with this FE slice.
evidence.feedTruth: CURRENT_MAIN requires provider/licensing entitlement evidence for realtime claims; no guaranteed sub-45ms SLO found.
evidence.securityTruth: CURRENT_MAIN implements CSP; public transport is HTTPS. MiCA is modeled as regulatory/governance guidance, not as a transport security standard.
